Wider Sports News.title: Postcard from Lausanne: What the SportAccord Forum revealed about the future of international sport
Wider Sports News.summary: From new hosting models to decentralised events, there was plenty on the agenda in Switzerland. The post Postcard from Lausanne: What the SportAccord Forum revealed about the future of international sport appeared first on SportsPro .
bullets: The 20th SportAccord Forum, rebranded from the IF Forum, took place from 5 to 7 October 2026 at the Olympic Museum in Lausanne, with SportsPro as exclusive content partner. Discussion covered the IOC's "Fit for the Future" strategy, under which the core Olympic programme will be confirmed seven years ahead from Brisbane 2032. Disciplines will be assessed on global appeal, cost, operational complexity and athlete representation, and IOC president Kirsty Coventry has said Brisbane will have fewer than the 36 sports in Los Angeles.

The IOC also published a Trustworthy AI Framework shortly before the Forum, while Halfspace's Sanjit Atwal argued that data should come before AI and that sport has been poor at using its data. SportsPro CEO Nick Meacham named participation as the biggest opportunity, citing over 1.3 million applicants for the 2027 London Marathon ballot and about 1.5 million Hyrox entries last season. The closing City Forum heard that cities increasingly want events to deliver for their communities, with public funding tied to priorities such as inclusion and sustainability.
Wider Sports News.copy:
It’s late on Sunday afternoon when SportsPro pulls into Lausanne on a train from Geneva, which means there’s only one place to aim for: the lake. Even as the sun is starting to set, there is still plenty of activity on the waterfront. As this correspondent (very) gently jogs along the path, periodically checking Google Maps to make sure he is still heading loosely in the direction of Saint-Sulpice, locals are still out on paddleboards, returning from tennis courts and passing a rugby ball between each other.

They don’t call this the Olympic Capital for nothing. After all, nearly 60 international sports organisations and federations are stationed in Lausanne and the surrounding Canton of Vaud, including the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

Wider Sports News.title: HSBC: 80 years of banking on the UAE’s ambition
Wider Sports News.summary: HSBC: 80 years of banking on the UAE’s ambition Gulf News
bullets: HSBC Bank Middle East chairman Abdulfattah Sharaf has marked the bank's 80th anniversary in the UAE, which dates from 12 October 1946, when a small branch opened beside Dubai Creek as the first bank in Dubai. It followed a meeting between Imperial Bank manager Frank Johnson and Sheikh Saeed Bin Maktoum Al Maktoum and his son, Sheikh Rashid Bin Saeed Al Maktoum.

The bank helped raise the loan to dredge Dubai Creek in 1954 and opened branches in Sharjah in 1953 and Abu Dhabi in 1959. It introduced the UAE's first operational ATM in 1984 and moved its incorporation and regional head office to the Dubai International Financial Centre in 2016. Sharaf points to green mortgages, the region's first digital bond with the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and mangrove restoration work, and closes: "We look forward to the next 80 years together."
Wider Sports News.copy:
On October 12, 1946, an international bank opened a small branch beside Dubai Creek. It was the first bank ever in Dubai. It was the result of a meeting between Frank Johnson, a manager of the Imperial Bank, with the late Sheikh Saeed Bin Maktoum Al Maktoum and his son, the late Sheikh Rashid Bin Saeed Al Maktoum. Johnson found rulers who already saw Dubai as a place the world would come to trade.

Eighty years on, that bank is HSBC Bank Middle East and the town it served is one of the world’s great centres of trade and finance. The partnership in Dubai began with infrastructure. In 1954, the bank worked to help raise the loan for dredging the Creek, the project that opened the city to larger vessels and set the pattern for the port-led growth that followed. As the Emirates grew, so did our presence: Sharjah in 1953, Abu Dhabi in 1959, and in time branches serving customers across the UAE.

Italy will face the Eagles again a week later in Nashville, Tennessee.

Rugby.title: Points pile-ups, old-school Saracens and a royal pint
Rugby.summary: After a try-filled round of action, how high can scoreboard inflation climb and what is behind it?
bullets: Northampton beat Bath 71-48 in round three of the Prem, ending Bath's unbeaten start to the season. The 18 tries and 119-point aggregate were the second highest in English top-flight rugby history, behind only Northampton's 94-33 win over Bristol in May. Five of the 10 top-flight games to pass 100 points have come since the start of 2023-24, and the round's five games produced 50 tries, an average of 10 per match.

Northampton head coach Sam Vesty attributed the scoring spike to stricter offside officiating, lower tackle height, game speed and fatigue, and greater attacking intent from teams. Elsewhere, Saracens beat Bristol 30-7 on a defence-led approach under coach Adam Powell, and Bristol rested three players over concerns about the artificial surface. Three of the five games were decided by seven points or fewer, and no side in the league remains unbeaten.
Rugby.copy:
It is worth taking a step back to fully appreciate the scale of scoring in the Prem currently. Ten seasons ago Northampton hosted Bath in round three. As on Saturday, Saints won to end Bath's unbeaten start to the season. The score then was 24-6.

Northampton scored four tries - from Courtney Lawes, George North and David Ribbans (twice). Bath had only two penalties from Rhys Priestland to show for their visit. This weekend it wasn't just a different game. It was like a different sport.

Rugby.title: WRU names businessman Faulkner as new chairman
Rugby.summary: Lyndon Faulkner, the nephew of Wales legend Charlie Faulkner, will take the role at the WRU's annual general meeting on 22 November.
bullets: The Welsh Rugby Union has named Lyndon Faulkner, a 66-year-old former Newport and Pontypool player, as its new chairman. He succeeds Richard Collier-Keywood and will take over at the WRU's annual general meeting on Sunday 22 November. Faulkner has built a business career in the United States, with senior roles at Microsoft and Pelican Products among others.

He takes up the role as the WRU plans to cut the professional tier from four teams to three, with Ospreys and Scarlets competing to avoid being surplus. Cardiff and the privately-backed Dragons have already been confirmed beyond the 2027-28 season. The WRU said his mandate is to lead strategic direction and hold the executive to account, and chief executive Abi Tierney said she and Faulkner are ready to form a formidable team.
Rugby.copy:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has named former Newport and Ponytpool player Lyndon Faulkner as the governing body's new chairman. The 66-year-old is the nephew of legendary Wales and Pontypool prop Tony "Charlie" Faulkner and has become a successful businessman in the United States since his playing days.

Faulkner will take over the role vacated by Richard Collier-Keywood at the WRU's annual general meeting on Sunday, 22 November. He will do so at a time when the WRU is planning to cut the game's professional tier from four to three teams, with west Wales sides Ospreys and Scarlets vying to avoid becoming surplus to requirements.

Rugby.title: Ex-Hurricanes Poua coach takes on key Fiji women’s rugby role
Rugby.summary: Former Hurricanes Poua head coach Fusi Feaunati has been named Head of Women's Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union.
bullets: Fusi Feaunati, the former Hurricanes Poua head coach, has been named Head of Women's Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union. He will connect the pathway from community rugby to the high-performance Fijiana Sevens and Fijiana XVs, working with academy staff, provincial and school coaches and community coaching programmes.

Feaunati was head coach of the Hurricanes Poua in Super Rugby Aupiki in 2025, having previously been an assistant. He was also women and girls lead at the Wellington Rugby Football Union and coached Wellington Pride in the Farah Palmer Cup. The union's General Manager High Performance, Naca Cawanibuka, said the appointment reflects the need to match the growth of women's rugby with stronger systems and support. The article cites 12 teams in the Subrails Marama competition and 16 in the Royal Tea Ranadi tournament.
Rugby.copy:
Former Hurricanes Poua head coach Fusi Feaunati has been named Head of Women’s Rugby by the Fiji Rakavi Football Union [FRFU]. The appointment follows growing interest and participation in women’s rugby across Fiji. Currently, 12 teams compete in the Subrails Marama competition, while 16 teams participate in the Royal Tea Ranadi tournament.

Feaunati’s role will focus on connecting the pathway from community rugby to the high-performance programmes of the Fijiana Sevens and Fijiana XVs. Feaunati said: “What excites me most about this opportunity is the ability to help shape a connected women’s rugby pathway across Fiji, from community and youth rugby through to elite international performance.

Rugby.title: Tom Willis steps up to dominate Top 14 in Jack's absence
Rugby.summary: Jack Willis may remain sidelined with a leg injury, but his brother, Tom, has ensured that the Willis family continues to wreak havoc on the Top 14.
bullets: Bordeaux-Bègles flanker Tom Willis made a match-high 18 carries and four turnovers as his side beat Clermont-Auvergne 23-22 at the Stade Marcel Michelin on Saturday. His late breakdown steal in his own 22 secured the win. The 27-year-old, who has eight England caps, came close to a try from a driving maul, but team-mate Maxime Lucu grounded the ball.

A try would have put Willis level with Pau's Rodrigo Marta on six for the Top 14 lead after six rounds. He was named in the team of the week by both Midi Olympique and L'Equipe. His brother Jack, Toulouse's reigning Top 14 Player of the Year, has been out with a thigh injury since round two. Bordeaux begin their bid for a third successive Champions Cup at Gloucester's Kingsholm on Friday 16 October.
Rugby.copy:
Jack Willis may remain sidelined with a leg injury, but his brother, Tom, has ensured that the Willis family continues to wreak havoc on the Top 14. The 27-year-old continued his barnstorming start to his second life at Bordeaux-Begles with a decisive role in his side’s 23-22 victory over ASM Clermont-Auvergne at the Stade Marcel Michelin on Saturday.

Tom made a match-leading 18 carries in the victory, and came close to scoring a try off the back of a driving maul, only for team-mate Maxime Lucu to take hold of the ball in the process of grounding it. Had the try been awarded to Tom, it would have lifted him to joint top of the try-scoring charts in the Top 14, level with Pau’s Rodrigo Marta with six in the opening six rounds.

Rugby.title: 'French Paul doesn't miss... I was just wondering what celebration he was going to pull'
Rugby.summary: The opening month of the 2026 Nations Cup delivered a stream of competitive, high-intensity games, multiple outstanding tries and set-piece battles...
bullets: Hong Kong China beat Uruguay at the World Rugby Nations Cup in July when winger Paul Altier kicked a penalty from about 40 metres, with no time left on the clock, to win the match. Team-mates said his confidence was at its highest after he landed almost every kick against Chile, and hooker Alexander Post, 30, said Altier "doesn't miss".

Former Northampton Saints and Bedford Blues player Matt Worley and Post both returned home after playing in England's Championship, which they regard as underrated. Hong Kong China have qualified for the men's World Cup in Australia, about 11 months away, and have reintroduced a full-time programme for more than 30 players. They face the USA, Canada and Tonga in November, hosting Tonga in their final game.
Rugby.copy:
'French Paul doesn't miss... I was just wondering what celebration he was going to pull' The opening month of the 2026 Nations Cup delivered a stream of competitive, high-intensity games, multiple outstanding tries and set-piece battles, and several great moments and memories that made July a successful start to the newly formed competition.

However, for Hong Kong China, their win over Uruguay tops everything else, as it came down to the final play. With no time left on the clock, the visitors squeezed out a penalty, and there was only one way forward: call for Paul Altier and ask their sharpshooter to send the ball through the posts.

Rugby.title: How the All Blacks left ‘waarheid’ behind at the Garden of Eden
Rugby.summary: The first Bledisloe Cup game between New Zealand and Australia provided further evidence that planet rugby is moving away from South Africa’s sphere of influence.
bullets: New Zealand won the first Bledisloe Cup Test 50-19 at Eden Park, Auckland, on Saturday. They hit their target of more than 100 rucks, lost under one per cent of possession to turnovers and increased ball-in-play time by over three minutes. Penalties fell, and scrum-half Cam Roigard's kicking and the use of double-team chases to contest high balls were singled out for improvement.

Writer Nick Bishop argues that rugby is splitting between South Africa's set-piece-led, physical approach and a faster, higher-scoring style used by most other teams. He notes the 2026 Six Nations produced a record 111 tries. The lineout still averaged about 83 per cent and the scrum was not truly tested, so he cautions against firm conclusions from one match. He suggests South Africa's style may still win another World Cup.
Rugby.copy:
There is the truth of the rugby world, and then there is the truth of South Africa. While the rest of the rugby world is dancing to the compulsive disco-beat under a glitterball of relentless attack, the world champions are waiting for the next World Cup and keeping their counsel; ready to pull the unwary back into the dark alleys outside and brawl with them in the gutter.

The 2026 Six Nations set a new record of 111 tries scored, and Les Bleus hardly noticed that they conceded the most tries [19] and points [130] of any winning campaign in the tournament’s history. The newly-minted Nations Championship in July promptly upped the ante, with an average of one extra converted try scored across the first three rounds.

Rugby.title: What Jason Gilmore says Harlequins 'can’t tolerate' as winless run continues
Rugby.summary: Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore claimed his side restored pride despite a third successive loss of the Gallagher Prem campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford.
bullets: Harlequins lost 28-24 to Sale Sharks at CorpAcq Stadium, their third successive Gallagher Premiership defeat. Sale won through a 73rd-minute penalty try, awarded after hooker Sam Riley was sin-binned for pulling down a maul illegally. Marcus Smith scored two tries on his return from injury and Riley also scored twice, while Sale replied through Elia Canakaivata, Gus Warr and Ben Bamber.

Head coach Jason Gilmore said his side had restored pride after a 48-0 loss to Gloucester the previous weekend and were pleased to earn two bonus points on the road. He said selection would depend on full commitment, adding "we can't tolerate" players being in one week and out the next. Harlequins are 10th with two points from three games. Sale are seventh on nine and play Glasgow next.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore claimed his side restored pride despite a third successive loss of the Gallagher Prem campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford. The Sharks snatched a 28-24 win with a 73rd-minute penalty try after they had been outplayed for long periods by a Quins side smarting from last weekend’s 48-0 humiliation against Gloucester.

“It’s disappointing. We probably created three chances in the first half which we didn’t take which came back to bite us,” said Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore. “Fair play to Sale. They got themselves back into the game with their set-piece but I’m really proud of the boys’ efforts up here.

Rugby.title: Rachel Malcolm challenges Scotland to end losing streak after Australia collapse
Rugby.summary: Scotland captain Rachel Malcolm wants her side to use the energy that will be generated around the quadruple header in Sydney on Saturday to their advantage and go out and put in a performance that they can be proud of.
bullets: Scotland captain Rachel Malcolm wants her side to use the atmosphere of a quadruple-header at Accor Stadium in Sydney on Saturday. Their WXV Global Series match against Australia's Wallaroos opens the day, ahead of two sevens matches and the second Bledisloe Cup Test. Malcolm said the players should enjoy the occasion without being overshadowed by it.

Scotland lost 30-10 to Australia at Hive Stadium on 26 September after leading 10-5 at half-time. Malcolm said the second-half collapse was a fair reflection of the result, and that rain left them with "a mountain to climb". Scotland, ninth in the world rankings, have lost seven Tests in a row, including earlier WXV defeats to Canada and New Zealand. Their campaign ends against the Wallaroos in Canberra on 23 October.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland captain Rachel Malcolm wants her side to use the energy that will be generated around the quadruple header in Sydney on Saturday to their advantage and go out and put in a performance that they can be proud of.

The WXV Global Series clash between the Wallaroos and the Scots will kick things off at the Accor Stadium and will be followed by a men’s sevens match between Australia and Fiji, a women’s sevens match between Australia and New Zealand and then the Wallabies against the All Blacks in the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026.

Rugby.title: Rob Baxter: 'That was bloody stressful and I agree with her'
Rugby.summary: Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter branded his side’s hard-fought victory over Newcastle which earned them a first Gallagher Prem victory of the season “bloody stressful”.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs beat Newcastle Red Bulls 34-28 at Sandy Park on 11 October for their first Gallagher Prem win of the season. Ross Vintcent scored two tries, with others from Sam Harris, Bachuki Tchumbadze and Henry Slade, who kicked three conversions and a penalty. Christian Wade scored a hat-trick for Newcastle, and Max Hicks also crossed.

Director of rugby Rob Baxter called the win "bloody stressful" and said his wife had said the same. He said Exeter lacked defensive energy and were slow to get up off the floor, but improved in the second half, conceding only one score. England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso left midway through the second half with a suspected hamstring overload and will be scanned. Newcastle's Dan McFarland said they made too many second-half errors, and his side play Scarlets away next.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter branded his side’s hard-fought victory over Newcastle which earned them a first Gallagher Prem victory of the season “bloody stressful”. Exeter were careless and error-strewn as the lead changed hands on numerous occasions at Sandy Park before they got their noses in front for the final time to clinch a 34-28 success in front of a disappointing crowd of just over 7,000.

Newcastle overcame an awful start, going behind after only 40 seconds, to make life extremely difficult for the home side, Christian Wade scoring a hat-trick of tries. Max Hicks added another, with Zack Henry converting all four to secure two valuable bonus points.

Rugby.title: Double Bok World Cup winner’s future hangs in balance as ruling looms
Rugby.summary: South Africa hooker Bongi Mbonambi is reportedly awaiting the outcome of a lengthy disciplinary hearing at the Sharks over alleged misconduct during a pre-season team-building camp in August.
bullets: Springboks hooker Bongi Mbonambi, 35, a double World Cup winner with 82 caps, is awaiting the outcome of a lengthy Sharks disciplinary hearing over alleged misconduct at a pre-season camp in August. Rapport reported the incident took place at Bayala Private Safari Lodges before the Sharks' 11 August fixture against the All Blacks. Mbonambi, Trevor Nyakane and Eduan Swart allegedly continued socialising into the following morning.

A ruling is expected within two weeks and reports suggest it could significantly affect his future. His contract runs to 2028 but could be terminated early. He has not played in the opening URC rounds, and coach JP Pietersen said there was "no comment on Bongi". He last played for South Africa against Wales in Cardiff in November. The ruling could affect his chances of a Test return in the November matches against Italy, Ireland and France.
Rugby.copy:
South Africa hooker Bongi Mbonambi is reportedly awaiting the outcome of a lengthy disciplinary hearing at the Sharks over alleged misconduct during a pre-season team-building camp in August.

According to South African outlet Rapport, the 35-year-old was involved in an incident at Bayala Private Safari Lodges before the Sharks’ August 11 fixture against the All Blacks. Head coach JP Pietersen had reportedly allowed players to socialise on a Tuesday evening before returning to full training, but Mbonambi, Trevor Nyakane and Eduan Swart allegedly continued into Wednesday morning.

Rugby.title: Exeter examine extent of Feyi-Waboso injury
Rugby.summary: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury he suffered in Exeter's win over Newcastle.
bullets: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury suffered in Exeter's 34-28 Prem win over Newcastle at Sandy Park, the Chiefs' first win of the season. The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half. He had started all three of Exeter's league games, scoring two tries at Bath the previous week.

Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter said he thinks Feyi-Waboso has overloaded the hamstring, that it is not catastrophic, and that it is more of a concern than a long-term worry. England host Australia, Japan and New Zealand in November in the second half of the Nations Championship. Feyi-Waboso missed this year's Six Nations with a hamstring injury and the second half of 2024-25 with a shoulder injury.
Rugby.copy:
England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will have a scan on a hamstring injury he suffered in Exeter's win over Newcastle. The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half of the 34-28 Prem win at Sandy Park - Exeter's first of the season.

He has started all three of the Chiefs' Prem games this season - scoring two tries at Bath last week. He started all three of England's Nations Championship games over the summer and crossed for tries against Fiji and Argentina.

Rugby.title: ‘I'm inspired’: Why an All Blacks veteran still draws inspiration from his younger brother
Rugby.summary: Speaking to New Zealand-based media from the All Blacks' hotel in Sydney, the 146-Test first-five admitted it was a special night at Eden Park for multiple reasons.
bullets: Beauden Barrett started his first Test of 2026 against the Wallabies at Eden Park, Auckland, alongside his brothers Scott and Jordie. It was the 54th time the three had played together at Test level. Beauden, a 146-Test veteran, said it was a special night and that playing with his brothers meant a lot after missing recent Tests.

Jordie was the All Blacks' man of the match with 16 tackles and 13 carries at No. 12, following strong performances in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series against South Africa. Beauden called him "hands down" the best No. 12 in the world at present and said he is inspired by his work rate and physicality. Scott, who has played 90 Tests, returned from a serious back injury after a non-playing sabbatical for the Crusaders.
Rugby.copy:
Running out alongside your two brothers for the All Blacks would be special enough once, let alone 54 times, but veteran playmaker Beauden Barrett continues to draw inspiration from his younger brothers.

Barrett started his first Test match of the 2026 season against the Wallabies at Eden Park, lacing up the boots alongside two of his younger brothers, Scott and Jordie, for the 54th time at Test level.

Rugby.title: Wade set to break Prem try-scoring record
Rugby.summary: Newcastle boss Dan McFarland is confident Christian Wade will break Prem Rugby's try-scoring record.
bullets: Christian Wade scored a hat-trick in Newcastle's 34-28 loss at Exeter, taking his career Prem try tally to 100. The 35-year-old former England winger needs one more to equal Chris Ashton's record of 101, set in April 2023. Newcastle boss Dan McFarland said he is confident Wade will break the record.

McFarland praised Wade's ability to connect with the squad, his pace and aerial ability, and the professionalism he gained from his time in the NFL. Wade scored most of his tries during seven years at Wasps before joining the Buffalo Bills in 2019, then moved to Racing 92 after his release in April 2022. He returned to England with Gloucester in 2024 and joined Newcastle in 2025. Exeter's Rob Baxter said his side defended Wade well but that Newcastle created good chances for him.
Rugby.copy:
Newcastle boss Dan McFarland is confident Christian Wade will break Prem Rugby's try-scoring record. The 35-year-old former England winger scored a hat-trick in Newcastle's 34-28 loss at Exeter to take his tally to 100 over his career.

Wade needs just one more try to equal Chris Ashton's record of 101, which was set in April 2023. "Christian is a really good man, an excellent connector," McFarland told BBC Sport.

Rugby.title: Exeter edge out Newcastle despite Christian Wade hat-trick
Rugby.summary: Exeter 34-28 Newcastle : A bottom of the table clash fell the way of the Chiefs
bullets: Exeter won their first Prem game of the season, beating Newcastle 34-28 at Sandy Park despite a hat-trick from Newcastle wing Christian Wade. The lead changed hands frequently and the Chiefs only sealed victory in the closing stages. Ross Vintcent scored two tries, with Sam Harris, Henry Slade and Bachuki Tchumbadze adding one each, and Slade kicked three conversions and a penalty.

Max Hicks scored Newcastle's other try, with Zack Henry converting all four to earn two bonus points. Newcastle led 21-19 at half-time, and full-back Jake Dalziel became the club's youngest ever league debutant at 18 years and 54 days. Exeter lost Immanuel Feyi-Waboso to a leg problem, and Newcastle prop Adam Brocklebank was sin-binned late on.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. A hat-trick from Newcastle wing Christian Wade was not enough to stop Exeter claiming their first Gallagher Prem win of the season as they edged a topsy-turvy game at Sandy Park 34-28.

The lead frequently changed hands and it was not until the dying stages that the Chiefs were able to seal victory. Max Hicks scored Newcastle’s other try, with Zack Henry converting all four to secure two valuable bonus points.

Rugby.title: Sale complete late win to leave Harlequins bottom of table
Rugby.summary: Sale 28-24 Harlequins: Marcus Smith’s tries threaten a schok result but Sale came back to win
bullets: Sale beat Harlequins 28-24 at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford, sealing victory with a 73rd-minute penalty try, to leave Quins bottom of the Prem after a third successive defeat. Marcus Smith, returning from a finger injury, scored two tries in the opening quarter, and Quins led 17-14 at half-time having had two tries disallowed.

Sale, who had lost on the opening day to Bristol, have now beaten Saracens and Harlequins in successive weeks, and it was their fifth straight win against Quins in the league and Europe. Jason Gilmore's side made seven changes after a 48-0 defeat by Gloucester, their worst league loss in 26 years. Hooker Sam Riley, who scored two tries, was sin-binned for the infringement that led to the penalty try.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Harlequins’ troubled start to the Gallagher Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium in Salford.

The Sharks left it late but came from behind to snatch a 28-24 success with a 73rd-minute penalty try, after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to threaten a shock win for the visitors.

Rugby.title: Late Sale penalty try continues Harlequins woes
Rugby.summary: Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continues with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium.
bullets: Harlequins lost a third successive Prem game, going down to Sale at CorpAcq Stadium after a 73rd-minute penalty try. Marcus Smith, back from a finger injury, scored two tries in the opening quarter, and Quins led 17-14 at half-time, with two further tries ruled out by the television match official. The result leaves Quins bottom of the table.

Sale, who also beat Saracens last week, scored through Elia Canakaivata, Gus Warr and Ben Bamber, and won with a rumbling maul that drove Quins back 30 metres. Referee Christophe Ridley awarded the penalty try and sent hooker Sam Riley to the sin-bin. Harlequins, beaten 48-0 by Gloucester the previous weekend, now face Vannes at home in the Challenge Cup next week.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium. The Sharks came from behind to win the game with a 73rd-minute penalty try after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to give Quins an early lead.

After their opening-day reverse to Bristol at home, Sale have bounced back strongly with back-to-back wins over Saracens and Quins. Despite their first points of the season, the loss leaves Quins rooted to the foot of the table.

Rugby.title: Wade scores 100th Prem try as Newcastle lose to Exeter
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade becomes just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 loss at Exeter.
bullets: Christian Wade became the second player to score 100 Premiership Rugby tries, claiming a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter. The 35-year-old scored twice in the first half, the second giving Newcastle a two-point half-time lead, and added a third early in the second half after a Henry Slade error. He is now one short of the all-time record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023.

Exeter secured a bonus-point first win of the season through tries from Ross Vintcent, who scored after 38 seconds on his return from injury, Sam Harris and Bachuki Tchumbadze, plus a 64th-minute Slade penalty. The result keeps Exeter eighth, four points behind leaders Gloucester, while winless Newcastle are second-from-bottom. A crowd of 7,071 meant Sandy Park's North Terrace was closed for the first time for a Prem game.
Rugby.copy:
Christian Wade became just the second player to score 100 Prem Rugby tries after getting a hat-trick in Newcastle Red Bulls' 34-28 defeat at Exeter. Wade, 35, went over twice in the first half - his second giving the Red Bulls a two-point half-time lead - before pouncing on a Henry Slade error to race in for a third early in the second half.

Newcastle's former England winger is now just one try off the all-time Prem try record of 101 set by Chris Ashton at Exeter in April 2023. Wade, who spent four years trying to break into the NFL from 2018, returned to the Prem in 2024 with Gloucester after two years at French side Racing 92, last year moving to Newcastle after a brief spell at rugby league's Wigan Warriors.

Rugby.title: Davies urged to reverse retirement for World Cup
Rugby.summary: Ex-Wales hooker Scott Baldwin is convinced the 36-year-old's World Cup know-how can still help Wales in Australia.
bullets: Former Wales hooker Scott Baldwin has urged scrum-half Gareth Davies to reverse his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup. Davies, 36, retired from Test rugby in 2024 but came off the bench to spark a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down against Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday, securing the club's first win of the season.

Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport that Davies could be valuable in a World Cup quarter-final against England, questioning Wales' depth behind Tomos Williams. Davies won 77 caps and toured twice with the British and Irish Lions, and will be 37 at the tournament, where Wales face Zimbabwe, Tonga and England in Pool F. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies praised his contribution as "superb".
Rugby.copy:
Gareth Davies has been urged to rethink his international retirement for the 2027 World Cup by former Wales team-mate Scott Baldwin. The 36-year-old scrum-half sparked a Scarlets comeback from 21-7 down to beat Benetton in the United Rugby Championship on Saturday.

Davies retired from Test rugby in 2024 but ex-Wales hooker Baldwin believes the veteran could still thrive at a fourth World Cup next year. "He could be just what you want in a quarter-final of a World Cup, in a Wales-England fixture in 12 months' time," Baldwin told BBC Radio Wales Sport.

Rugby.title: Fight for Wales spots heats up as under-threat regions win
Rugby.summary: The talking points from round three of URC as Ospreys and Scarlets get first win and players try to impress Wales boss Steve Tandy.
Rugby.copy:
There was western relief after Ospreys and Scarlets got up and running in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) season. The two sides are playing amid uncertainty over their futures under controversial Welsh Rugby Union plans, yet produced the goods on the pitch in round three.

Ospreys won an engrossing derby against Dragons at Rodney Parade, inflicting a first defeat of the season on their hosts, while Scarlets sneaked past Benetton thanks to Sam Costelow's late penalty.

Rugby.title: Ulster playing games like training sessions
Rugby.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach Richie Murphy says Ulster are "playing matches like they're training sessions" as he expressed his disappointment with his side's slow start in Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.

Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.

Rugby.title: Leinster stroll past Cardiff for happy homecoming
Rugby.summary: Champions Leinster score five tries to beat Cardiff in Dublin for their first win of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship campaign.
Rugby.copy:
Champions Leinster made a successful return to the revamped Laya Arena by beating Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship (URC). The Irish province recorded their first victory of the 2026-27 season in front of 20,600 supporters, and condemned the Blue and Blacks to a first loss.

Leinster scored three tries inside the first quarter through Hugo Keenan, Jimmy O'Brien and Jack Conan, then O'Brien's second in the 37th minute secured the four-try bonus. But, with a raft of Ireland internationals making their first outings of the campaign, the second half was flat and scoreless until Jamie Osborne went over with five minutes to go.

Rugby.title: Caluori scores as Saracens too strong for Bristol
Rugby.summary: Noah Caluori gets on the scoresheet as Saracens continue their hold over Bristol Bears at the StoneX Stadium with a 30-7 victory.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: Caluori, O'Driscoll, penalty, J. Bracken Cons: Farrell Pens: Farrell 2 Saracens continued their hold over Bristol Bears at the StoneX Stadium with a convincing 30-7 victory.

Bristol have now failed to win in all eight of their Prem visits to Saracens' home since they reached the top flight, with this loss also their first defeat of the 2026-27 campaign.

Rugby.title: Edinburgh top URC after bonus-point win over Zebre
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh go top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre makes it three wins from three.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: M. Currie, Douglas, Bradbury, T. Currie Cons: Grayson 3 Pens: Grayson Edinburgh went top of the nascent United Rugby Championship table as a bonus-point victory at Zebre made it three wins from three for Sean Everitt's injury-hit side.

Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz described his level of play in his shock defeat to Zizou Bergs at the 2026 Shanghai Masters as “really bad” as he also made a comment about his opponent’s “luck.”

The world No 3 suffered a 5-7, 6-7(4) loss to world No 39 Bergs on Monday in the third round at the ATP 1000 tournament in China. Alcaraz was making his first appearance at the Shanghai Masters since 2024 after he missed last year’s event due to injury.

Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz fell to a surprise third round defeat to Zizou Bergs at the Shanghai Masters. The Spaniard struggled with the conditions in Shanghai against Bergs and the Belgian ultimately made him pay to race to a 7-5, 7-6 victory at the Masters tournament.

Alex Eala’s recent struggles continued after she was dumped out of the Wuhan Open by world No 201 Han Shi in the first round. Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz opens up on ‘negative thoughts’ after surprise Shanghai Masters defeat

bullets: Carlos Alcaraz lost 7-5, 7-6(4) to 27-year-old Belgian Zizou Bergs in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Monday at the Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena. The world No 3 had won the ATP 500 event in Tokyo the previous week, his first title since returning from a wrist injury that kept him out for more than four months. Afterwards he said his mind was full of negative thoughts and that he was unhappy with almost everything about his play. He plans to review the match with his coach and team, and remains optimistic about the rest of the season.
Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz says it is “really difficult” to take any positives from his straight-set loss to Zizou Bergs at the Shanghai Masters. After winning his first title since returning from a wrist injury at the Japan Open last week, Alcaraz was much more sluggish against an inspired Bergs on Monday.

The Belgian was not overawed by the occasion and closed out a 7-5, 7-6 (4) third-round victory. The 27-year-old served for the match at 6-5 but was broken back immediately to set up a tiebreak.

Carlos Alcaraz’s miserable record at the Shanghai Masters continued as he was beaten in the third round by Zizou Bergs. Tennis.title: Zverev secures year-end number one ranking

bullets: Alexander Zverev is guaranteed to finish 2026 as world number one after Carlos Alcaraz lost 7-5 7-6 (7-4) to Belgium's Zizou Bergs in the Shanghai Masters third round on Monday. Current number one Jannik Sinner is out for the rest of the year with a knee injury. Zverev, 29, will become the first German man to end a year top of the rankings and the oldest to do so for the first time.

Zverev won his first Grand Slam title at the French Open in June and added the US Open last month, both without having to face Sinner or Alcaraz. He cannot overtake Sinner until 2 November at the earliest. Alcaraz, back after almost five months out with a wrist injury, said he did not feel good, while Bergs faces Tommy Paul in the last 16.
Tennis.copy:
Alexander Zverev is guaranteed to finish the 2026 season as world number one after Carlos Alcaraz's surprise defeat in the Shanghai Masters. German Zverev was on course to climb above current world number one Jannik Sinner, who has been ruled out for the rest of the year with a knee injury.

Alcaraz still had a mathematical chance of stopping Zverev until he was beaten 7-5 7-6 (7-4) by Belgium's Zizou Bergs in the third round on Monday. "It's been a fantastic season for me. Knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," said Zverev.

Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz’s campaign at the 2026 Shanghai Masters ended with a shock third round defeat, but how has the result impacted the ATP Rankings? The seven-time Grand Slam champion fell to a 7-5, 7-6(4) upset loss to 39th-ranked Zizou Bergs at the Masters 1000 tournament in Shanghai on Monday.

Alcaraz’s exit ended his six-match ATP Tour winning streak that included his second round victory in Shanghai and his successful title defence at the Japan Open earlier this month.

Tennis.copy:
Alexander Zverev says it is a “dream come true” that he will finish 2026 as the year-end No 1. With Jannik Sinner out for the rest of the season with a knee injury, Zverev was destined to finish the year as the world’s top-ranked player.

However, Carlos Alcaraz’s surprise third-round loss to Zizou Bergs at the Shanghai Open means nobody can catch the 29-year-old in the ATP Tour rankings. The German has enjoyed a magical year, winning both the French Open and US Open to finally break his Grand Slam duck. Now, the 6ft 6in player has opened up on a “fantastic” season that is getting better and better.

Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz vs Zizou Bergs controversy sparks calls for major tennis rule change after ‘unacceptable’ incident
Tennis.summary: "How is that allowed?" The post Carlos Alcaraz vs Zizou Bergs controversy sparks calls for major tennis rule change after ‘unacceptable’ incident appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Zizou Bergs, 27, beat second seed Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6(4) in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Monday at the Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena. The match lasted just over two hours and was the biggest win of Bergs' career. He said he often has too much respect for opponents, which he described as part of his culture, and now sees he can beat players like Alcaraz.

Jamie Murray criticised Bergs for a bathroom break of nearly 10 minutes after the first set. Journalist Jose Moron cited the ATP rulebook, which allows three minutes plus two for a clothing change, and said Bergs took about nine and a half minutes without a chair umpire warning. Murray noted the walk to the changing rooms should take about 20 seconds. Brad Gilbert said such breaks happen too often and suggested limiting them to set breaks, with a point lost for every 30 seconds of delay.
Tennis.copy:
Zizou Bergs secured an unforgettable victory over Carlos Alcaraz at the Shanghai Open but the Belgian has been criticised for his actions during the third-round match. Bergs upset second seed Alcaraz in just over two hours in a 7-5, 7-6 (4) victory at Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena on Monday for the biggest win of his career.

The 27-year-old was, naturally, emotional after this major scalp, particularly as he has struggled to get over the line in big matches. He said afterwards, “This is something that has been very tough for me. I often have too much respect for these guys, which is part of my culture and I’m proud of that. But it gets a little bit in the way when you have to play them. I had a great moment here last year against [Novak] Djokovic where I was definitely playing the name, not the guy.

Carlos Alcaraz was dumped out in the third round of the Shanghai Masters as Zizou Bergs recorded the biggest win of his career, with the Spaniard's defeat confirming Alexander Zverev as the year-end world No 1.

Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz struggled in his third-round match against Zizou Bergs in the third round of the Shanghai Masters. The Spaniard arrived at the penultimate Masters tournament of the calendar in good form, having lifted the Japan Open title for the second year in a row.

Tennis.title: Zizou Berg’s immediate reaction after stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz in Shanghai
Tennis.summary: Zizou Bergs stunned after stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz. The post Zizou Berg’s immediate reaction after stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz in Shanghai appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Zizou Bergs, 27 and ranked world No 39, beat seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6 in just over two hours in the third round of the Shanghai Masters. Tennis.copy:
Zizou Bergs was not quite sure “what was going on” after his stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz at the Shanghai Masters, admitting he was in “disbelief”. The world No 39 claimed the biggest win of his career as he beat seven-time Grand Slam winner Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6 (7-5) in just over two hours in the third round of the ATP Masters 1000 event.

It is only his third top-10 win following victories over world No 9 Andrey Rublev at the 2025 Miami Open and world No 5 Felix Auger-Aliassime at this year’s United Cup. Alcaraz was the overwhelming favourite as he is fresh from winning the Japan Open and also cruised past Juan Manuel Cerundolo in the second round, but never got his nose in front as the Belgian broke in game five before the second seed got back on terms in the next game.

Elena Rybakina maintains a healthy lead in the rankings ahead of Aryna Sabalenka while Mirra Andreeva has cracked a new career-high and Zheng Qinwen surged 31 places. Three-time Grand Slam winner Rybakina started her fourth week at No 1 in the WTA Rankings on Monday and her second-round exit from the China Open didn’t cost her too much as her main rival Aryna Sabalenka also didn’t fare well.

Tennis.copy:

Just hours after delighting her fans by winning her maiden WTA 1000 title, the China Open on home soil in Beijing, Zheng confirmed that she won’t feature in the second leg of the double-header in Wuhan.

Sonay Kartal says she has "thrown herself in the deep end" since returning from a six-month injury absence after beating Anhelina Kalinina to reach the Wuhan Open second round.

Tennis.copy:
Olympic champion Qinwen Zheng made history as the first Chinese player to win the China Open on Sunday, stunning French Open winner Mirra Andreeva 7-5 6-4. Wild card Zheng, who has been on a recovery path after missing nearly six months due to an elbow injury on her dominant right arm, looked like her old self as she used powerful forehands to control the rallies, and landed swift winners angling away from Andreeva.

After the two exchanged early breaks, world No 5 Andreeva held firm to go 5-4 up, and almost got a decisive break when Zheng sent a cross-court shot too long before netting a forehand.

bullets: Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open, beating fourth seed Mirra Andreeva 7-5 6-4 in Beijing on Sunday. Entering as a wildcard ranked 54th in the world, the 24-year-old saved three set points in the opener, then won the remaining 11 points of the set. She sealed victory with an ace and sang karaoke for the home crowd after her victory speech.

It was Zheng's first WTA 1000 title and sixth overall, ending a two-year title drought for a player who underwent elbow surgery last year. The win was her 14th over a top-10 opponent. Zheng said she had been through a very tough year and had found her fire again. Andreeva, 19, is expected to rise to number three, while Zheng is set to climb 31 places to number 23.
Tennis.copy:
Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open by beating Mirra Andreeva in Beijing. Zheng, who entered the tournament as a wildcard ranked number 54 in the world, saved three set points in Sunday's opener before overcoming fourth seed Andreeva 7-5 6-4.

The 24-year-old fell to the floor after converting match point and treated the raucous home crowd to some karaoke following her victory speech. "The feeling was incredible. To win here in Beijing in front of my home crowd is one of my dreams," she said.

Golf.title: Are Your Iron Shafts Too Heavy? The Small Gear Change That Saved This 8 -Handicapper's Game
Golf.summary: In my experience, up to 70% of golfers play iron shafts that are too heavy - here is how one simple gear change completely transformed a hapless 8-handicapper's game...
Golf.copy:
Over my years as a PGA Professional, I’ve custom-fit thousands of golfers, seeing virtually every swing type and equipment mismatch imaginable. But every now and then, a single tweak yields results so transformative it genuinely stops you in your tracks.

That exact scenario played out recently with my good friend and Kick Point podcast co-host, Dan Parker... Dan is a fairly typical 8-handicap player with a pretty solid all-round game, but having played together on numerous occasions, I had long felt that the 120-gram steel shafts in his Ping i230 irons were just far too heavy for him. On the course, he always seemed to be struggling to catch his arms and clubhead up to his body turn through impact. The inevitable result was a frustratingly inconsistent strike and dangerously unpredictable start directions.

Golf.copy:
Which players are leaving LIV Golf? And who is sticking around for the league’s 2.0 era? This is everything you need to know… The deadline for LIV Golf players to decide whether they will stick or twist is almost here.

The league has until October 25 to convince key names to sign up for the new iteration of the league ahead of a possible $300 million investment from credit firm BC Partners. And it is crucial that the league persuades some big hitters to stay for its relaunch. But the DP World Tour’s move to reject memberships for players who hope to sign up to LIV 2.0 has made LIV’s prospects a whole lot more difficult.

Golf.title: DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players for 2027, ending their Ryder Cup eligibility
Golf.summary: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings told BBC Sport that players who participate in LIV Golf 2.0 won't be allowed to play on the European circuit. The post DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players for 2027, ending their Ryder Cup eligibility appeared first on Golf .
bullets: DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings told BBC Sport that the European circuit will no longer grant conditional releases to LIV players in 2027, saying "players need to make a choice". The earlier agreements, which let players such as Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton keep their Ryder Cup eligibility, applied only to the 2026 season. Players will now be asked to disclose which tours they intend to play, and any who sign a deal and then play LIV would have their membership terminated.

The deadline to apply for DP World Tour membership is 16 November, while players must commit to LIV Golf 2.0 by 25 October. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew funding, and BC Partners has since agreed to back the relaunch as part of a targeted $300 million in cumulative financing, subject to court approval. The ban comes as the DP World Tour renegotiates its alliance with the PGA Tour, and the next hearing in LIV's bankruptcy case is on Wednesday 14 October.
Golf.copy:
Whatever becomes of LIV Golf 2.0, the DP World Tour has decided it won’t let those who compete in the rebel circuit’s new version have it both ways. In a statement to BBC Sport, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said the European circuit, which had previously reached agreements with LIV players to allow them into its tournaments, will no longer do so in 2027, effectively banning them from playing.

“Players need to make a choice,” Kinnings told BBC Sport. “We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour.”

Golf.title: 'I'm dejected': Late bogeys cost promising pro PGA Tour card
Golf.summary: Cole Hammer had one hand on a 2027 PGA Tour card before a poor final round at the Korn Ferry Tour Championship left him "dejected." The post ‘I’m dejected’: Late bogeys cost promising pro PGA Tour card appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Cole Hammer, 27, missed out on a PGA Tour card at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship after a final-round 73 left him tied 43rd. He began the week 20th in the season-long standings, the last position that earns a card, but five Sunday bogeys, including one on his second-to-last hole, dropped him to 22nd. David Lamb, who started the week 23rd, finished 20th to take the final card.

Hammer, who helped Texas win the 2022 NCAA title and was named the world's best amateur in 2019, said ball striking let him down and that he was "dejected". He added that he still believes in himself and described his pursuit of a card as "a fun journey" of five or six years of learning. He will play another season on the Korn Ferry Tour.
Golf.copy:
Sunday saw a host of young and journeyman pros alike experience the highlight of their careers: earning PGA Tour cards at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship. As happens every year, heartwarming tales about players’ big achievements abound. But there is another side to the story: the other pros who just missed out on their Tour cards.

On Sunday, the pain that group felt was best exemplified by Cole Hammer. The 27-year-old Texas pro narrowly lost his grasp on his own Tour card with a poor final round on Sunday. But instead of fleeing the course as fast as he could, a “dejected” Hammer faced the cameras and opened up about his unfortunate fate. In the process, he showed a hard-earned perspective that should serve him well as he continues his pro career.

Golf.title: Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win
Golf.summary: Scotland's Grant Forrest holds off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year.
bullets: Scotland's Grant Forrest held off home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open, earning a place at The Open and the Masters next year. Chacarra was in the clubhouse on 13 under, so Forrest and Victor Perez needed birdies at the 18th. After Perez's putt drifted past, Forrest holed his to claim a third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Forrest began the final round sharing the lead with England's Joe Dean on 13 under. He made bogeys at the third, sixth and eighth but recovered with three birdies and a bogey in five holes at the start of the back nine. A closing one-under 70 earned the £480,000 first prize. Forrest said he was in pure shock after a tough year and could not believe he was going to Augusta.
Golf.copy:
Scotland's Grant Forrest held off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year. With Chacarra in the clubhouse at 13 under, Forrest and playing partner Victor Perez needed to make birdies at the 18th to go above the Spaniard.

Both players' drives nestled down in the greenside rough on the 322-yard par four, and after Perez's birdie putt drifted past the hole, Forrest sunk his to seal his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Golf.title: How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson

bullets: Alistair Docherty, 32, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time in 2027, told this week's GOLF Subpar podcast that his first golf memory was the 2010 U.S. Senior Open at Sahalee Country Club in Sammamish, Washington. He attended with his father and they sat by the 10th tee.

Bernhard Langer hit his tee shot into one of the course's many evergreens there. Docherty said he told his father that pros hit bad shots too. Langer went on to win that week, which taught Docherty that one bad shot does not determine the outcome. Sahalee also hosted the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.
Golf.copy:

Sahalee is a private country club in Sammamish, Wash., just outside of Seattle, and in 2010 it hosted the U.S. Senior Open. (It was also home to the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.) But in 2010, Docherty attended the U.S. Senior Open with his father, and they found a spot to sit by the 10th tee.

Forrest lost the 2015 Amateur Championship final 4&2 to Romain Langasque, which cost him a Masters place. His earlier DP World Tour wins came at the 2021 Hero Open and the 2025 Nexo Championship. Golf.copy:
Eleven years ago, Grant Forrest had a ticket to the Masters in his grasp. Then a budding Scottish amateur star, Forrest reached the finals of the 2015 Amateur Championship. A win meant not only one of amateur golf’s biggest prizes but also a trip to Magnolia Lane. But a 4&2 loss to Romain Langasque meant Forrest’s Augusta National dream would have to wait.

The wait wasn’t expected to be long. Forrest made the 2015 Walker Cup team and was expected to be one of Europe’s bright young stars. But golf had other plans. Forrest turned pro and worked his way up from the Challenge Tour to the DP World Tour, finally reaching the top European circuit in 2019. His first DP World Tour win arrived at the 2021 Hero Open. His next came four years later at the 2025 Nexo Championship. Along the way, Forrest played in two Open Championships and one U.S. Open, but never played well enough to reach Augusta National.
